entries.summary: Two fronts opened and one stalled. In the US, Mylan/Viatris filed a declaratory-judgment suit in D. Del. on Sep 25 seeking to invalidate or design around US Patent 12,551,536 — a method-of-administering patent on single-dose Wegovy pens that runs to October 2038 — which is about clearing a device/method overhang rather than accelerating entry, since compound patents still block US semaglutide generics until 2032. In India, Novo widened its offensive from injectables to oral semaglutide: the Delhi High Court barred Sun Pharma from launching semaglutide tablets without prior court permission, and Novo is asserting a follow-on formulation patent live to roughly 2031 against Dr Reddy's, Sun and Torrent. The 14 tirzepatide Paragraph IV suits filed Aug 6 showed NO verifiable procedural progress — a tool-access limitation, not evidence nothing happened.
entries.content:
August 10 - September 28, 2026 patents and IP:

1. MYLAN/VIATRIS OPENS A NEW US FRONT ON WEGOVY DEVICE/METHOD PATENTS (Sep 25)
   - Mylan Pharmaceuticals Inc. (a Viatris unit) sued Novo Nordisk in the DISTRICT OF DELAWARE seeking
     a DECLARATORY JUDGMENT that US Patent No. 12,551,536 is invalid or not infringed by its generic
   - That patent covers A METHOD OF ADMINISTERING SINGLE-DOSE WEGOVY PENS for weight loss, EXPIRING
     OCTOBER 2038
   - Docket: Mylan Pharmaceuticals Inc. v. Novo Nordisk Inc. et al., No. 1:26-cv-01192 (D. Del.)
   - *** STRATEGIC READ: US semaglutide generics still CANNOT enter until the COMPOUND patents expire
     in 2032. So this suit is about clearing a DEVICE/METHOD OVERHANG that would otherwise extend
     exclusivity 6 years past compound expiry - not about accelerating entry. ***
   - Novo booked nearly $31bn from Wegovy plus Ozempic in the prior year

2. INDIA - NOVO WIDENS FROM INJECTABLES TO ORAL SEMAGLUTIDE
   a) DELHI HIGH COURT BARS SUN PHARMA FROM LAUNCHING SEMAGLUTIDE TABLETS (Aug 11-12)
      - Justice Anup Jairam Bhambhani directed that IF Sun Pharma obtains a licence to commercially
        manufacture semaglutide tablets, it must INFORM THE COURT AND OBTAIN ITS APPROVAL before taking
        any further step toward market launch
      - Novo alleged Sun had cleared the Subject Expert Committee for 3 mg, 7 mg and 14 mg semaglutide
        tablets and that these infringe its patent on semaglutide tablets, arguing a post-launch
        withdrawal would be impractical
      - NO patent number or case number is stated in the available coverage - none published here
   b) THE STRUCTURAL SPLIT THAT MATTERS
      - The semaglutide COMPOUND patent EXPIRED 2026-03-20 - injectables are free, hence 33+ brands
      - The ORAL/TABLET FORMULATION route is STILL CONTESTED
      - IAM reports Novo's disputes have broadened to oral tablets on a FOLLOW-ON PATENT still active
        for roughly five more years (i.e. ~2031), in the Delhi High Court against Dr Reddy's, Sun
        Pharma and Torrent
      - Prior coverage identifies the relevant formulation patent as IN 325669, covering SNAC
        (sodium N-(8-(2-hydroxybenzoyl)amino) caprylate), the absorption enhancer in oral semaglutide,
        valid to 2031. *** That patent number is CARRIED OVER from earlier coverage, NOT from the
        in-window article, which is paywalled beyond the standfirst. Treat accordingly. ***

3. STATUS OF THE 14 TIRZEPATIDE PARAGRAPH IV SUITS FILED AUG 6 - NO VERIFIED MOVEMENT
   - NOT ONE answer, consolidation order, scheduling order or settlement could be verified as entered
     between Aug 10 and Sep 28, 2026
   - The filings themselves (Aug 6-7 2026, D. Del., against Sandoz, MSN Laboratories and others,
     following Paragraph IV notices Lilly disclosed in its Aug 5 quarterly filing) are the Aug 10
     baseline, not new
   - *** A third-party tracker states the Sandoz case is Eli Lilly & Co. v. Sandoz Inc.,
     No. 1:26-cv-00987 (D. Del.), filed Aug 6 2026, with ten patents asserted and a November 13 2029
     stay-related deadline reflecting the NCE-1 rule. THE TRACKER EXPLICITLY DISCLAIMS having
     re-verified the docket, and neither the case number, the ten-patent count nor the 2029 date could
     be independently confirmed - CourtListener and Justia both returned HTTP 403.
     DO NOT PUBLISH 1:26-cv-00987 OR NOV 13 2029 AS VERIFIED. ***
   - CourtListener, PACER-backed docket pages and Law360 full text were all inaccessible to the
     available tools. THIS GAP IS A TOOL-ACCESS LIMITATION, NOT EVIDENCE THAT NOTHING HAPPENED.
     A PACER or Docket Navigator pull is needed to close it.

4. VERIFIED NEGATIVES FOR THIS WINDOW
   - PTAB / IPR: NO NEWS. No IPR petition or institution decision on any semaglutide, tirzepatide or
     liraglutide patent surfaced.
   - ORANGE BOOK listings/delistings: NO NEWS.
   - INDIAN PATENT OFFICE decisions, pre-/post-grant oppositions, Section 3(d), compulsory licensing:
     NO NEWS. The only India IP developments were the Delhi High Court items above.
   - EPO oppositions / China CNIPA / Federal Circuit appeals / trade-secret and API-process disputes /
     patent term extensions: NO NEWS. The China Supreme People's Court semaglutide compound-patent
     affirmation was 2025-12-31 and the Dutch injunction 2026-08-05 - both outside the window.

5. LILLY FILES SIX SUITS AGAINST RETATRUTIDE GREY-MARKET SELLERS (Aug 12) - NOW VERIFIED
   *** UPGRADED 2026-09-28 from 'unverified lead' to VERIFIED: retrievable sources were subsequently
   confirmed - BioPharma Dive (https://www.biopharmadive.com/news/lilly-lawsuit-retatrutide-black-market-obesity-drug/827659/)
   and Endpoints News (https://endpoints.news/eli-lilly-files-first-lawsuits-over-retatrutide-black-market/),
   both 2026-08-12. ***
   - Six suits against online merchants, clinics, compounders and foreign suppliers selling purported
     retatrutide - a drug still INVESTIGATIONAL, whose BLA Lilly does not plan to file until Q1 2027
   - Lilly warned the material could be fake, impure or mis-dosed
   - Backdrop: in July 2026 an FDA advisory panel endorsed broader use of six peptides without
     substantial safety/efficacy evidence; compounders retained share even after FDA declared the GLP-1
     shortage over
   - *** THIS IS ENFORCEMENT AGAINST UNAPPROVED-PRODUCT SELLERS, NOT HATCH-WAXMAN ANDA LITIGATION. It
     does NOT touch tirzepatide or semaglutide generic timelines. Still no case or patent numbers
     verified - none published. ***

6. REMAINING UNVERIFIED LEAD - NOT PUBLISHED AS FACT.
   - A compounding pharmacy moved to dismiss Novo Nordisk's semaglutide patent suit (Law360,
     2026-08-25), part of the campaign Novo launched in D. Del. in February 2026 asserting its
     semaglutide API patent against compounded injections and pills. The MOTION, not a decision. No
     case number, patent number or ruling verified.

entries.summary: The tirzepatide patent cliff litigation began. Lilly's 10-Q disclosed receiving Paragraph IV notices in July, then filed 14 ANDA suits in D. Delaware on August 6 asserting nine patents including US 9,474,780. Novo separately opened Hatch-Waxman proceedings against Cipla and Apotex (July 17/21, consolidated) and sued Viatris in W.D. Pa. on August 7. Novo also won a Dutch preliminary injunction against a compounding pharmacy where the enforcement basis was SPC 300936 — valid to March 2031, surviving the March 2026 compound-patent expiry. CORRECTION: the dashboard has been carrying Teva v. Novo as the live US semaglutide case; no in-window Teva activity was found, and the actual live cases are Novo v. Cipla and Novo v. Apotex.
entries.content:
July–August 2026 patents/IP:

1. ⭐ TIRZEPATIDE HATCH-WAXMAN — 14 SUITS (Aug 6)
   - Lilly 10-Q verbatim: 'In July 2026, Lilly received notice that multiple generic companies had filed ANDAs seeking approval to market generic versions of Mounjaro and/or Zepbound before the expiration of some or all of the patents listed for those products in the FDA's Orange Book. We intend to file suit for patent infringement.'
   - Filed D. Del. Aug 6: 1:26-cv-00972, -973, -974, -976, -977, -978, -980, -981, -982, -984, -985, -986, -987, -988 (NOS 835 ANDA, cause 35:271)
   - Defendants: Alembic, Amneal, Aspiro, Biocon, Dr. Reddy's, Eugia, Galenicum, Hikma, Hybio, Macleods, MSN, Rio Biopharmaceuticals, Sandoz, Zydus
   - Patents asserted: 9,474,780 (GIP/GLP-1 co-agonist compounds), 11,357,820, 11,918,623, 12,295,987, 12,343,382, 12,453,755, 12,453,756, 12,453,758, 12,616,740
   - 30-month stay expected

2. NOVO US SEMAGLUTIDE LITIGATION
   - Hatch-Waxman proceedings commenced against CIPLA and APOTEX (Jul 17 and Jul 21), consolidated in June 2026
   - Novo's Q2 report confirms Cipla notified it of an ANDA with Paragraph IV certifications; complaint filed in D.N.J.
   - Apotex already holds a US tentative approval (Apr 2026) — classic first-filer-blocked-only-by-patent posture
   - NEW: Novo Nordisk Inc. v. Viatris Inc. filed W.D. Pa. Aug 7 (2:26-cv-01667)
   - ⚠️ CORRECTION: No in-window Teva v. Novo activity found across multiple query formulations. The dashboard's framing of Teva as the live US semaglutide ANDA case should be softened — the actual live cases are Novo v. Cipla and Novo v. Apotex.

3. NOVO WINS DUTCH PRELIMINARY INJUNCTION (Aug 5)
   - District Court The Hague, C/09/704955 / KG ZA 26-494, against Ceban Ziekenhuisfarmacie (compounding semaglutide nasal spray)
   - Novo asserted Dutch SPC 300936 (valid to 19 March 2031) alongside compound patent EP 1 863 839 (expired March 2026) — THE SPC IS WHAT CARRIES ENFORCEMENT PAST COMPOUND EXPIRY
   - Court read the pharmacy exemption NARROWLY: resale to other pharmacies, stockholding and G-Standard registration all fell outside it
   - Ceban must cease distribution, delist, and disclose suppliers; penalties to €500,000

4. NOVO v. LILLY — FALSE ADVERTISING (Jul 21)
   - D.N.J. 3:26-cv-09027, Chief Judge Zahid N. Quraishi, cause 15:1125 Lanham Act, jury demanded
   - Novo alleges Lilly 'engaged in false advertising and unfair competition in connection with their dissemination of nationwide, direct-to-consumer advertising campaigns related to the comparative efficacy of FDA-approved GLP-1 medicines'
   - Seeking permanent injunction and corrective advertising; Novo escalating with a bid to halt the ads
   - Branded-vs-branded, not compounding — but the marquee GLP-1 legal event of the window

5. OFA v. FDA — STILL UNDECIDED
   - 5th Cir. Nos. 25-10600 and 25-10758; argued March 30, 2026 before Judges Richman, Duncan, Oldham
   - Only in-window docket activity is administrative: entries 150–151 (Jul 7) substituting Acting Commissioner Kyle Diamantas for Marty Makary in the caption
   - Neither docket terminated; no merits ruling

6. INDIA — NO IN-WINDOW RULINGS
   - Delhi HC: no new decisions on Novo's secondary/formulation suits vs Torrent and Dr Reddy's. All located decisions predate the window (single-judge Dec 4 2025; Division Bench dismissal ~Mar 9 2026 on Patent 262697; Torrent interim arrangement Mar 21 2026; Natco revocation petition Jan 2026)
   - India tirzepatide patent status unchanged; Mounjaro + Cipla Yurpeak licensed duopoly intact to ~2033–2036

7. RESOLVED BEFORE WINDOW (housekeeping)
   - Novo v. Hims & Hers: voluntarily dismissed Mar 9, 2026, replaced by a commercial collaboration. No in-window developments.

entries.content:
June 2026 patent/IP landscape:

1. TIRZEPATIDE PARAGRAPH IV (US) — MILESTONE PASSED:
   - Eligibility window opened May 13, 2026 (4 years after Mounjaro approval)
   - As of June 24, 2026: NO public ANDA filings disclosed in FDA Orange Book
   - Lilly's 21-patent fortress remains intact
     - Primary composition patent: expires January 2036
     - Formulation patents: extend to 2039-2041
     - Device patents (Mounjaro KwikPen): additional protection
   - First-filer incentive (180-day exclusivity) makes filing attractive once any generic challenger believes it has invalidity case
   - Industry expectation: filing could come Q3-Q4 2026 but not necessarily public until ~90 days into court process

2. INDIA SEMAGLUTIDE (post March 20 patent expiry):
   - Novo's primary composition patent expired March 20, 2026
   - Novo's SNAC/granule formulation patent infringement suits in Delhi HC vs Torrent, Dr Reddy's:
     - Initial ex parte injunction DENIED pre-expiry
     - Subsequent suits continuing on merits
     - No interim injunctions granted
   - 50+ generic semaglutide brands operational in India
   - Dr Reddy's oral Obeda Tablets launched May 20 (oral generic semaglutide)
   - Delhi HC's evergreening rejections continue to set precedent

3. INDIA TIRZEPATIDE — CRITICAL CLARIFICATION:
   - Tirzepatide India patent expiry: ~2033-2036 (NOT NOW)
   - Current Indian market: Mounjaro (Lilly) + Cipla Yurpeak ONLY (duopoly)
   - Both priced ₹3,500-₹4,375/weekly injection
   - Generic tirzepatide entry in India: not expected for ~7-10 years
   - Indian regulatory pathway: SND (Subsequent New Drug) requires Phase 3 in Indian patients
   - Yurpeak is Cipla's LICENSED brand under Lilly partnership, NOT generic

4. TEVA-NOVO US SEMAGLUTIDE (Delaware District Court):
   - Teva Hatch-Waxman Paragraph IV challenge to US9,694,053
   - Initial proceedings continuing
   - Decision not expected before late 2027
   - If Teva prevails on obviousness: US semaglutide generic entry could accelerate from 2031-2032 to 2028-2029

5. MFN DEAL AS PATENT POLICY:
   - Trump MFN deal effectively a 'soft march-in rights' mechanism
   - Extracts pricing concessions without invoking formal compulsory licensing
   - Reduces political urgency for accelerating generic entry through patent challenges
   - But does NOT change underlying patent expiry dates

6. PATENT CLIFFS — UPCOMING:
   - Semaglutide India: EXPIRED March 2026
   - Tirzepatide US Para IV eligibility: OPENED May 13, 2026
   - Semaglutide US: 2031-2032 (per Novo composition patent + extensions)
   - Tirzepatide US: 2036 (composition) / 2039-2041 (formulations)
   - Tirzepatide India: ~2033-2036
   - Liraglutide globally: Expired 2024-2025 (mostly)

7. SECONDARY PATENT JURISPRUDENCE:
   - Delhi HC continues evergreening rejection pattern (Section 3(d))
   - US Teva challenge tests obviousness over GLP-1 analogs
   - I-MAK analysis: Novo holds 320 US semaglutide applications (154 granted) — patent thicket strategy

entries.content:
May 2026 patent landscape update — tirzepatide Paragraph IV milestone:

1. THE MAY 13, 2026 MILESTONE:
   - Tirzepatide (Mounjaro/Zepbound) becomes eligible for Paragraph IV patent challenges on May 13, 2026 — exactly 4 years after initial Mounjaro FDA approval (May 13, 2022).
   - Para IV allows generic manufacturers to file ANDAs challenging Lilly's tirzepatide patents.
   - As of May 10, 2026, no public ANDA Para IV filings have been disclosed in the FDA Orange Book.

2. LILLY'S PATENT FORTRESS:
   - 21 active US patents on tirzepatide.
   - Primary composition patent: expires January 2036.
   - Formulation patents: extend protection to 2039-2041.
   - Device patents (Mounjaro KwikPen): additional protection.
   - Lilly's patent strategy is more concentrated than Novo's semaglutide thicket but each individual patent is harder to invalidate.

3. OUTLOOK:
   - Even if Para IV filings emerge May 13+, meaningful US generic tirzepatide competition before 2036 is considered remote.
   - The Novo-Teva semaglutide litigation precedent (initial proceedings, decision 2027+) suggests tirzepatide Para IV cases would resolve no earlier than 2028-2029.
   - India tirzepatide market: Lilly launched Mounjaro in March 2025; patent expiry in India follows the 20-year rule, so 2036+.
   - China tirzepatide: Patent expiry 2036+.

4. SEMAGLUTIDE LITIGATION CONTINUING:
   - Teva's Hatch-Waxman Para IV challenge to US9,694,053 (semaglutide composition) continues in Delaware District Court.
   - Initial proceedings scheduled; decision not expected before late 2027.
   - If Teva prevails on obviousness, US semaglutide generic entry could accelerate from 2031-2032 to 2028-2029.

5. INDIA PATENT TRACKING:
   - Delhi HC continues to reject Novo's secondary patent claims (microsphere formulation challenge ruled against Novo).
   - Sun Pharma joined Dr Reddy's in HC export approval (April).
   - Section 3(d) evergreening jurisprudence reinforced.

6. ACTION FOR LEADERSHIP:
   - Track FDA Orange Book directly for tirzepatide ANDA Para IV filings after May 13.
   - Monitor Teva-Novo Delaware proceedings.
   - Watch for any India High Court rulings on tirzepatide secondary patents.

entries.summary: April 2026 patent update: The Delhi HC continues to reject Novo Nordisk's secondary patent claims. Sun Pharma received export clearance joining Dr Reddy's. A companion Novo microsphere formulation patent challenge is pending — setting a precedent on evergreening in Indian pharma. Globally, tirzepatide's Paragraph IV eligibility window opens May 13, 2026, but no ANDA filings public yet. Teva's biosimilar semaglutide litigation continues in US District Court (Delaware).
entries.content:
April 2026 patents/IP landscape:

1. DELHI HC EVERGREENING STANCE: After denying Novo's ex parte injunction pre-expiry, the Delhi HC has reinforced its position on evergreening. A separate Novo Nordisk secondary patent covering a microsphere formulation was challenged by generics and ruled "falls flat" — drawing a hard line against patent extension via incremental innovations that lack enhanced therapeutic efficacy (Section 3(d) criteria).

2. SUN PHARMA EXPORT NOD: Sun Pharma received Delhi HC approval to export semaglutide in April 2026, following Dr Reddy's earlier clearance. This opens Canada, Brazil, Turkey, and other post-patent markets to Sun Pharma's Noveltreat/Sematrinity portfolio.

3. TIRZEPATIDE PARA IV (US): Tirzepatide becomes eligible for Paragraph IV patent challenges on May 13, 2026 — exactly 4 years after Mounjaro's initial approval. No ANDA filings are public yet. Eli Lilly's 21-patent fortress (primary composition to 2036, formulations to 2039-2041) makes meaningful generic competition before 2036 unlikely.

4. TEVA-NOVO US LITIGATION: Teva's Hatch-Waxman Paragraph IV challenge to US9,694,053 (semaglutide composition) continues in the US District Court (Delaware). Initial proceedings scheduled; decision not expected before late 2027. If Teva prevails on obviousness over GLP-1 analogs, US semaglutide generic entry could accelerate from 2031-2032 to 2028-2029.

5. MFN DEAL AS POLICY PRESSURE: Trump's MFN pricing deal effectively acts as a "soft march-in rights" mechanism — extracting pricing concessions without invoking formal compulsory licensing. This may reduce the political urgency around accelerating generic entry through patent challenges.

entries.summary: The Delhi High Court denied Novo Nordisk's emergency ex parte injunction request just before the March 20, 2026 semaglutide patent expiry, allowing Torrent's generic to launch hours ahead of the product patent's expiration. No secondary/formulation patent provided any additional protection. 50+ brands are expected across 40+ manufacturers in 2026. Novo Nordisk's India IP strategy shifts post-expiry to trade dress, quality differentiation, and Wegovy HD (7.2mg) — the only dose not yet replicated by generics.
entries.content:
The India patent situation for semaglutide resolved decisively against Novo Nordisk as of March 20, 2026. Key developments:

1. DELHI HIGH COURT: Novo Nordisk sought an ex parte injunction (emergency order without hearing the other side) to block generic entry ahead of the patent expiry. The Delhi High Court denied this request, directing only an interim solution rather than a full injunction. Torrent Pharmaceuticals received a green light to launch generic semaglutide hours before the product patent's official March 20 expiry date — effectively becoming the first company to market.

2. SECONDARY PATENTS: Unlike in the US, where Novo holds 154 granted patents creating a dense thicket around Ozempic/Wegovy, India's secondary patent landscape did not provide Novo with meaningful protection beyond the primary compound patent. No device, formulation, or dosing patents created barriers to entry for Indian generic manufacturers. This contrasts sharply with the US where secondary patents extend protection to 2035.

3. MARKET ENTRY: The complete absence of injunctive relief contributed to the rapid Day 1 entry of 15+ generic manufacturers. 50+ brand names are expected across 40+ manufacturers by end of 2026, representing one of the most competitive generic market entries in Indian pharmaceutical history.

4. NOVO'S POST-EXPIRY IP STRATEGY: With the compound patent expired and no secondary patent protection, Novo Nordisk's IP strategy has shifted to: (a) Trade dress protection for Ozempic/Wegovy pen design and packaging; (b) Data exclusivity periods for specific approved indications; (c) First-mover advantage in Wegovy HD (7.2mg) — the high-dose formulation approved by FDA in March 2026 that does not have a corresponding Indian generic approval and represents the only dose not yet replicated by competitors.

5. GLOBAL CONTEXT: Semaglutide patents have now expired in India, China, Brazil, Canada, and Turkey — markets covering 40% of the world's population. Tirzepatide (Mounjaro/Zepbound) becomes eligible for US Paragraph IV patent challenges on May 13, 2026, though meaningful US generic competition remains unlikely before 2036.

entries.summary: I-MAK analysis reveals Novo Nordisk has filed 320 US patent applications and been granted 154 patents for Ozempic/Wegovy/Rybelsus — creating a patent thicket estimated to extend US exclusivity to 2031-2032 and potentially earning Novo $166 billion in US exclusivity profits. Production cost studies show semaglutide could be profitably manufactured for $0.89-$4.50/month.
entries.content: I-MAK's deep-dive into GLP-1 drug patent abuse provides critical context for understanding the gap between production economics and market pricing. Novo Nordisk has filed 320 US patent applications and been granted 154 US patents related to semaglutide products (Ozempic, Rybelsus, Wegovy). These patents create a thicket that extends US exclusivity far beyond the original compound patent, with the most recent patents expiring in 2035. A parallel analysis found that semaglutide could be profitably manufactured for between $0.89 and $4.50 per month — compared to the US list price of $936-$1,349/month, representing a 200-1,500x price markup above profitable production cost. The patent thicket is estimated to generate $166 billion in US exclusivity profits for Novo Nordisk between 2026 and 2031. Eli Lilly has a smaller but still significant portfolio: 53 US patent applications and 16 granted patents for tirzepatide. I-MAK's analysis contributed to congressional discussions about GLP-1 pricing and the Biden/Trump administration's inclination toward invoking march-in rights or accelerating IRA price negotiations for GLP-1 drugs. The US patent barrier remains the primary reason generic semaglutide is available at $14/month in India but $900/month in the US.

entries.summary: The 2026 GLP-1 patent cliff now spans India, China, Brazil, Canada, and Turkey — covering 40% of the world's population. China's semaglutide patent also expired in March 2026. Tirzepatide becomes eligible for US Paragraph IV challenges on May 13, 2026, though meaningful US generic competition remains unlikely before 2036 given Eli Lilly's 21-patent fortress.
entries.content: The 2026 GLP-1 patent cliff is more geographically concentrated than previously understood. India and China's semaglutide patents both expired in March 2026, while Brazil and Turkey expired earlier in 2026, and Canada in January 2026. Collectively, these markets cover approximately 40% of the world's population — creating a two-tier global GLP-1 market where innovator pricing applies in US/EU ($900-$1,350/month) but generic pricing dominates everywhere else ($15-$50/month). Dr. Reddy's plans to launch generic semaglutide in 87 countries in 2026, starting with Canada, India, Brazil, Turkey, and other emerging markets. A key milestone: tirzepatide (Mounjaro/Zepbound) becomes eligible for Paragraph IV patent challenges in the US on May 13, 2026 — exactly 4 years after Mounjaro's US approval date. However, Eli Lilly's tirzepatide patent fortress is formidable: 21 US patents cover the molecule, with the primary composition patent expiring January 2036 and formulation patents potentially extending protection to 2039-2041. No generic tirzepatide challenge has been filed as of March 2026, and meaningful US competition before 2036 is considered remote. The M&A angle: GeneOnline reports that the $100B+ GLP-1 patent cliff has triggered a global M&A race, with large pharma companies acquiring biosimilar capabilities and pipeline molecules to position for the post-exclusivity era. Russia's compulsory licensing approach, Brazil's rejection of Novo's patent extension request, and WHO's recommendations for tiered pricing and pooled procurement signal increasing government pressure on GLP-1 pricing globally.

entries.summary: The US District Court for the District of Delaware scheduled initial proceedings in Novo Nordisk's patent infringement suit against Teva over its biosimilar semaglutide filing.
entries.content: The US District Court for the District of Delaware scheduled initial proceedings in Novo Nordisk's patent infringement suit against Teva over its biosimilar semaglutide filing. Teva is challenging the core composition patent (US9,694,053) under Hatch-Waxman Paragraph IV, arguing obviousness over prior GLP-1 analogs. A decision is not expected before late 2027.

entries.summary: The Indian Patent Office heard arguments in the ongoing Section 3(d) challenge to Novo Nordisk's semaglutide patent. A ruling is expected by mid-2026.
entries.content: The Indian Patent Office heard arguments in the ongoing Section 3(d) challenge to Novo Nordisk's semaglutide patent. Generic manufacturers argued that semaglutide represents incremental modification of the known GLP-1 analog liraglutide without demonstrating significantly enhanced therapeutic efficacy as required under Indian patent law. A ruling is expected by mid-2026.

entries.summary: Semaglutide's patent landscape reveals a critical 6-year gap between India and US patent expiry: India's compound patent expired March 20, 2026 (strict 20-year term with no extensions), while US protection extends to December 2031 via Patent Term Adjustment and Extension.
entries.content: Semaglutide's patent landscape reveals a critical 6-year gap between India and US expiry. India follows a strict 20-year patent term with no extensions under TRIPS, leading to expiry on March 20, 2026. In the US, the main compound patent (US8,129,343) benefits from Patent Term Adjustment and Patent Term Extension, pushing expiry to December 2031. Novo Nordisk holds 154 granted US patents across its three semaglutide products (Ozempic, Wegovy, Rybelsus), creating a dense patent thicket. The company is projected to earn an estimated $166 billion from continued US exclusivity between 2026 and 2031, while markets covering 40% of the world's population open to generic competition in 2026.

entries.summary: India's Section 3(d) of the Patents Act prevented Novo Nordisk from evergreening its semaglutide patent, with the Delhi High Court allowing Dr. Reddy's to continue manufacturing and recognizing the challenge as prima facie valid.
entries.content: India's Section 3(d) of the Patents Act proved instrumental in enabling generic semaglutide competition. The Delhi High Court rejected Novo Nordisk's attempt to enforce a second patent, ruling that it represented potential double patenting and lacked true innovation under Section 3(d). Dr. Reddy's was allowed to continue manufacturing and exporting semaglutide. This decision builds on the precedent set by the landmark 2013 Novartis Glivec case and signals that India's patent framework strongly disfavors incremental modifications of known molecules. Over 40 Indian manufacturers capitalized on this ruling to prepare generic launches for the March 20, 2026 patent expiry.

entries.summary: Eli Lilly's tirzepatide (Mounjaro/Zepbound) is protected by 21 US patents with the primary compound patent expiring in January 2036, but formulation patents could extend protection as far as 2041.
entries.content: Eli Lilly's tirzepatide is shielded by a dense patent portfolio of 21 US patents and one FDA Regulatory Exclusivity. The key composition of matter patent (US9,474,780) expires in January 2036, while additional composition patents extend to September 2031 and January 2037. Formulation patents further restrict generic launch until potentially 2039-2041. Mounjaro becomes eligible for Paragraph IV patent challenges on May 13, 2026, though meaningful generic competition is not expected before 2036 at the earliest. This gives Eli Lilly a decade-long head start over generic competitors, contrasting sharply with semaglutide's more vulnerable patent position.

entries.summary: Teva and Galenicum Health successfully challenged Novo Nordisk's European semaglutide obesity patent at the EPO, which revoked the patent for lacking an inventive step, while additional challenges targeted oral semaglutide (Rybelsus) patents.
entries.content: Teva and Galenicum Health secured a major victory at the European Patent Office, which revoked Novo Nordisk's European patent on semaglutide use in a specific dosage for treating obesity, ruling it lacked an inventive step. Separately, the EPO's Boards of Appeal revoked two patents important for semaglutide tablet administration (Rybelsus) following challenges by Teva, Galenicum, Generics Ltd, and Hexal. In Canada, Sandoz, Apotex, and Teva filed generic applications immediately after patents expired on January 4, 2026. At least three US companies have filed Paragraph IV certifications, though settlements with Novo Nordisk suggest US generics remain unlikely before 2032.

entries.summary: Russia has already invoked compulsory licensing for semaglutide under Article 1360 of its Civil Code, while WHO's strategies for expanding GLP-1 access include both voluntary and compulsory licensing mechanisms for developing countries.
entries.content: Russia has taken the most aggressive approach to GLP-1 access, invoking compulsory licensing for semaglutide under Article 1360 of its Civil Code. Meanwhile, WHO's December 2025 obesity guideline explicitly recommends strategies including compulsory licensing, pooled procurement, and tiered pricing to expand access in developing countries. Brazil denied Novo Nordisk's request for patent extension, opening its market to generic competition from March 2026 with local manufacturer Biomm partnering with India's Biocon. In price-sensitive markets where patents expired in 2026 (India, China, Brazil, Turkey), monthly therapy costs are projected to fall to $40-50, compared to $300+ in the US. The patent cliff across markets covering 40% of world population marks the beginning of a structural price reset for GLP-1 therapies.
